Each agent is scored by the median number of distinct, mutually non-adjacent neighbors that route through it over a rolling window; new identities enter at a low depth tier. To reach full economic privileges, an identity must appear as a stable waypoint on many independent paths—clustering returns a low atlas score, not a high one. Building one credible path costs the attacker sustained traffic and infrastructure on separate network segments; faking breadth requires multiplying that cost across every forged node.
